200: Holy Corpse Rising by Hosana Tanaka (Seven Seas) is a dark action-horror fantasy with a touch of harem comedy. In an alternate 15th-century Rome where witches wage war on humanity, young monk Nikola Eskalibur, orphaned by a witch, discovers he can revive twelve sealed First Witches. The catch is that each one must be bound to him by a marriage contract. It's a fast, gothic read for fans of monster battles, witches, and blood-and-faith fantasy.
201: Behind The Scenes by Bisco Hatori (Viz Media) is a warm, goofy campus comedy with a light romantic thread. Ranmaru Kurisu, a timid college freshman who apologizes for everything, stumbles into the Art Squad, a ragtag crew that builds props, sets, and special effects for student films. Among these passionate misfits, he starts to find a place where he belongs. It's a cheerful read for fans of Ouran High School Host Club and anyone who loves stories about making things together.
202: Honey Hunt by Miki Aihara (Viz Media) is a glossy showbiz romance and drama. Yura Onozuka has always lived in the shadow of her famous actress mother and celebrated composer father. When her family falls apart in a very public way, the shy teen decides to step into the entertainment world herself and make a name of her own. It's a juicy, emotional read for fans of celebrity drama, love triangles, and heroines finding their nerve.
203: How I Met My Soulmate by Anashin (Kodansha) is a sweet, grounded shojo romance. After a long dry spell, Tokyo college sophomore Yuuki, who dreams of meeting her soulmate, lets a friend drag her to a loud club that's nowhere near her comfort zone. There she meets Iori, a bleached-blond guy with an intimidating air, and starts to wonder whether fate has something in store for her. It's a cozy pick for readers who like realistic love stories with adult characters.
204: The Princess of Convenient Plot Devices by Mamecyoro (Yen Press) is a playful fantasy romance light novel. Maki Tazawa, a devoted boys' love fan, is reborn into her favorite BL novel as Princess Octavia, whose only role in the plot is to produce a royal heir. She adores the story's central couple but refuses to be a mere plot device, so she sets out to find a love and happy ending of her own. It's a witty read for fans of villainess and reincarnation stories.
205: Hunting In Another World With My Elf Wife by Jupiter Studio (Seven Seas) is an outdoorsy isekai fantasy with a romantic streak. Professional hunter Shin Nakajima is killed by a bear and wakes up in another world armed with nothing but his shotgun. When wolves attack, he's rescued by Saran, a skilled elf huntress, and the two quickly form a bond. It's a down-to-earth read for fans of survival skills, hunting know-how, and slow-burn fantasy companionship.
206: Black Sun Silver Moon by Tomo Maeda (Go! Comi) is a gothic supernatural action story. To pay off his late father's debt to the church, eighteen-year-old Taki Juhas goes to work for the mysterious priest Shikimi. By day he does chores around the church; by night the two of them destroy the dead who rise from their graves. It's a moody, atmospheric read for fans of zombies, exorcists, and prickly partnerships.
207: I Belong to the Baddest Girl at School by Ui Kashima (One Peace Books) is a goofy school romantic comedy. Timid Unoki is used to being pushed around, so when Toramaru, the most feared delinquent in school, decides he's hers, he nervously goes along with it. What he doesn't realize is that the scary girl genuinely likes him and wants a sweet, normal romance; she just has no idea how to show it. It's a light, funny read for fans of tough-girl, soft-boy pairings.
208: Blood Alone by Masayuki Takano (Infinity Studios) is a quiet, moody supernatural mystery with a tender heart. In Yokohama, former vampire hunter Kuroe Kurose now makes his living as a private detective and writer. He shares his home with Misaki, a young girl who was recently turned into a vampire, and his cases often pull them into run-ins with the undead. It's a gentle, atmospheric read for fans of slow-burn relationships and soft-spoken urban fantasy.
209: I Wanna Do Bad Things With You by Yutaka (Viz Media) is a mischievous coming-of-age romantic comedy. Mamori Wataya, a tall, plain girl who keeps to herself, befriends Soushi Fuji, the most disliked boy at school, when he asks her to help him drain the school pool. Soon she's his sidekick in a string of pranks against the school and the people who look down on them. It's a funny, sweet read for anyone who's ever felt like an outsider.
210: Blood Sucker by Saki Okuse (Tokyopop) is a dark supernatural action story with art by Aki Shimizu. Yusuke Himukai sets out to rescue his beloved Kikuri from Migiri, an ancient vampire who has been revived with help from his loyal servant and has claimed Kikuri as his bride. What follows is a tense fight against vampires steeped in Japanese myth. It's a solid pick for fans of gothic horror, rescue quests, and moody vampire lore.
211: The Star Seekers by HYBE (Yen Press) is a fantasy idol drama with plenty of action. In an entertainment world where magic-wielding performers dominate, Star One is a group of five boys who never developed powers and are struggling to stay relevant. When mysterious terrorists attack a magic-powered idol show the group is filling in for, one member suddenly awakens his abilities and saves the day. It's an energetic read for K-pop fans and anyone who enjoys underdog stories.
212: If I Could Reach You by tMnR (Kodansha) is a quiet, bittersweet yuri drama. High schooler Uta lives with her older brother and his wife, Kaoru, who was once her childhood friend and first crush. After a year under the same roof, Uta starts noticing cracks in their marriage, and as she becomes Kaoru's main source of comfort, her old feelings return. It's a gentle, emotional read for fans of slow, introspective romance and complicated family ties.
213: Penguin Revolution by Sakura Tsukuba (CMX) is a bright showbiz comedy with a cross-dressing twist. Yukari Kikuchi has a rare gift: she can tell at a glance whether someone has the potential to become a star. Hired by a talent agency, she must disguise herself as a boy to work as manager for up-and-coming actor Ryo Ayanokoji. It's a lighthearted, funny read for fans of mistaken identity, entertainment-industry stories, and sweet shojo romance.
214: The Valiant Must Fall by Yu Aida (Seven Seas) is a dark historical action drama. After the fall of the Tokugawa shogunate, Haruyasu, a former samurai lost in a changed world, wants nothing more than a death that brings him peace. His attempt to assassinate a government official leaves him at the mercy of the man's bodyguard, a young woman who claims to be the daughter of an immortal and wants something in return for sparing him. It's a gripping, bloody read for fans of samurai stories.
215: The Vampire and His Pleasant Companions by Narise Konohara (Yen Press) is a quirky supernatural comedy with art by Marimo Ragawa. Albert Irving is a vampire of strict habits, sleeping by day and flitting around as a bat by night, until an accident at a Nebraska meat-processing plant gets him flash-frozen and shipped to Japan. He wakes up in Tokyo naked, unable to speak Japanese, and forced to rely on a few bewildered new companions. It's a charming, offbeat read for fans of fish-out-of-water humor.
216: Can't Lose You by Wann (Net Comics) is a romantic drama built on a classic switched-places premise. Yooi, a penniless high school girl, juggles several jobs to pay off her father's debts, while Lida, born into a wealthy and powerful family, chafes against the rules that come with her name. When the two meet and discover they look exactly alike, Yooi agrees to step into Lida's life as her double. It's an engaging read for fans of mistaken identity and Cinderella-style romance.
217: Inukami! by Mari Matsuzawa (Seven Seas) is a rowdy supernatural comedy with plenty of fan service, adapted from Mamizu Arisawa's light novels. Keita Kawahira comes from a family whose members team up with inukami, powerful dog spirits, but none of them wanted anything to do with him. The only one who did is Yoko, a beautiful inukami with a jealous streak and a talent for chaos. It's a goofy, high-energy read for fans of spirit-partner comedies and the anime.
218: Those Not-So-Sweet Boys by Yoko Nogiri (Kodansha) is a charming high school romantic comedy. On her first day of high school, studious Midori drops her wallet and is helped by Ichijo, one of a trio of boys who never come to class. When the school board chairman catches her working a part-time job against school rules, he makes her a deal: he'll look the other way if she can get those three boys back in class. It's a sweet, easygoing read for fans of classic shojo.
220: President Dad by Ju-Yeon Rhim (Tokyopop) is a lighthearted Korean comedy with a romantic streak. Ordinary high school freshman Ami Won's life turns upside down when her father is elected President of South Korea. With her mother gone, Ami is pressured to take on the role of first lady, all while a bodyguard shadows her at school disguised as a classmate. It's a breezy, funny read for anyone who enjoys school comedy mixed with fish-out-of-water family chaos.
221: Kami Kaze by Satoshi Shiki (Tokyopop) is a dark, violent seinen action fantasy. A thousand years ago, five elemental warriors sealed away 88 monstrous beasts, but the beasts cursed three of them so that their descendants would one day set them free. In present-day Japan, Misao Mikogami, the Maiden of Water whose blood can open the prison, is drawn into the fight by Kamuro Ishigami, the Warrior of Earth. It's an intense read for fans of brutal supernatural battles.
222: Kamichama Karin Chu by Koge-Donbo (Kodansha) is a sparkly magical-girl comedy and the sequel to Kamichama Karin. Clumsy, big-hearted Karin Hanazono, who can transform into a goddess with the help of a magic ring, returns alongside her friends Kazune and Himeka for a new round of divine trouble. The story mixes slapstick, sweet crushes, and bigger magical stakes than before. It's a cheerful, fast-moving read for fans of the first series and classic magical-girl manga.
223: Colorless by KENT (Seven Seas) is a gritty, stylish sci-fi action story. A cosmic disaster has drained all color from the Earth, and humanity has mutated until few people still look human. In this bleak urban world, Avidia, a lone-wolf investigator armed with his wits and a powerful gun, hunts for the last hidden traces of color, until he meets a girl who may hold the key to restoring what was lost. It's a striking read for fans of noir atmosphere and inventive worldbuilding.
224: Confidential Confessions by Reiko Momochi (Tokyopop) is a serious, unflinching shojo drama. Each volume tells standalone stories about Japanese teenage girls facing hard realities such as abuse, self-harm, compensated dating, and illness. The stories treat their subjects frankly but with real compassion for the girls caught up in them. It's an emotional, thought-provoking read for older teens and adults who appreciate realistic stories about difficult issues.
225: Crescent Moon by Haruko Iida (Tokyopop) is a romantic fantasy adventure with art by Taraku Uon. Mahiru Shiraishi is an ordinary girl with an extraordinary gift: her tears can reveal the hidden Tears of the Moon. That makes her invaluable to a band of thieves from the Lunar Race, including the prickly tengu Mitsuru, who need her help to recover the scattered gems. It's a sweet, lighthearted read for fans of yokai, treasure hunts, and slow-building shojo romance.
226: Cross by Sumiko Amakawa (Tokyopop) is a dark supernatural action story steeped in exorcism and religious imagery. Takara Amakusa is a young Catholic priest who drives out demons with a sign of the cross that burns on his forehead, a power that costs him dearly every time he uses it. When Shizuha, a girl whose body can bear ancient scripture, is targeted by demons and a cult her own parents have joined, she turns to him for help. It's a moody pick for fans of exorcist manga.
227: Raiders by JinJun Park (Yen Press) is a gory, fast-paced action fantasy manhwa. Irel Clark, a professor's assistant, stumbles onto a relic tied to the blood of Christ, and to save his own life he drinks from it. He becomes immortal, but the world around him is soon overrun by undead cannibals, and his new body makes him their favorite target. It's a hard-hitting read for fans of zombie action, religious relics, and over-the-top battles.
228: Re-Living My Life with a Boyfriend Who Doesn't Remember Me by Eiko Mutsuhana and Gin Shirakawa (Seven Seas) is a bittersweet time-loop fantasy romance. Seventeen-year-old magic student Oriana dies alongside her boyfriend, Vincent, then wakes up in her seven-year-old body with her memories intact. When she finds Vincent again, he has no idea who she is, so she sets out to win his heart a second time and avoid the fate that awaits them. It's a heartfelt read for fans of second-chance love stories.
229: Twittering Birds Never Fly by Kou Yoneda (SuBLime) is a dark, adult boys' love yakuza drama. Yashiro is a flamboyant, provocative yakuza boss who takes on Doumeki, a quiet young man fresh out of prison, as his new bodyguard. As the two grow closer, Yashiro's tangled past and the dangers of his world complicate everything between them. It's an intense, emotionally layered read for mature fans of BL who appreciate crime stories and complicated characters.
230: Kazan by Gaku Miyao (ComicsOne) is a desert fantasy adventure with a hopeful heart and a melancholy edge. Young Kazan's village is destroyed and his childhood friend Elsie kidnapped by a mysterious water-wielding invader. Ten years later, he's a bandit who still looks like a child, traveling with his white eagle Kamushin, when he rescues Fawna, a girl who can also summon water. It's a thoughtful, adventurous read for fans of classic fantasy quests and stories about growing up.
231: King of Cards by Makoto Tateno (CMX) is a lighthearted card-battle comedy. High schooler Manami Minami is new to the trading card game Chaos when she lands Saghan the Mighty Sorcerer, an ultra-rare card that's supposedly out of print. Suddenly every Chaos player in Japan wants to win it from her in a duel. With help from her cousin and her friends and rivals, she learns the game while juggling everyday school life. It's a fun pick for fans of card-game manga.
232: Welcome Back, Alice by Shuzo Oshimi (Kodansha) is a quiet, unsettling coming-of-age drama. High schooler Yohei Miyamoto is reunited with his childhood friend Kei, who returns with a new look and announces a wish to be neither a boy nor a girl. The change throws Yohei's feelings, and the friendships around them, into confusion he never expected. It's a thoughtful, intimate read for fans of Oshimi's psychological stories and nuanced explorations of identity and desire.
233: La Esperança by Chigusa Kawai (DMP) is an elegant, emotional boarding-school drama with a shonen-ai thread. Georges Saphir is the model student at Saint Grollo Boys' School, working hard to be everything his cruel father is not. His carefully kept image starts to crack when Robert Jade, a rebellious transfer student, begins needling him and challenging his innocence. It's a thoughtful, beautifully drawn read for fans of European-style settings, slow-building friendships, and introspective coming-of-age stories.
234: Land of Silver Rain by Mira Lee (Net Comics) is a gentle Korean folklore fantasy with a touch of romance. Abandoned as a baby in a cabbage patch, Misty-Rain is rescued by a witch and raised among the Dokebi, magical beings far from any human. Her peaceful life ends when she loses her guardian's trust, the magic hiding her true identity breaks, and she is sent out into the human world she was born into. It's a charming read for fans of fairy-tale adventures.
236: Little Queen by Yeon-Joo Kim (Tokyopop) is a lively magical-school fantasy with plenty of rivalry. June Narcieq attends Rohini Royal Academy, where children with magical potential are trained and the most gifted girls are groomed as candidates to become the Queen of Light. June finds herself competing with her rival, Lucia Luferr, both for the crown and for their childhood friend, Sejuru Ney. It's a fun, energetic read for fans of spellcasting academies, love triangles, and spirited heroines.
237: Doubt!! by Kaneyoshi Izumi (Viz Media) is a breezy high school romantic comedy. Teased as a plain "monkey" in middle school, Ai Maekawa reinvents herself as a glamorous, popular girl when she starts high school. Keeping up the new image is harder than it looks, especially once the cool and blunt Sou Ichinose sees right through her. It's a fun, stylish read for fans of makeover stories, sharp-tongued love interests, and classic shojo romance.
238: Seaside Stranger by Kanna Kii (Seven Seas) is a gentle, sun-soaked boys' love romance. Shun, a young gay man who left home after coming out, is living quietly on a small island in Okinawa when he meets Mio, a local high schooler who seems drawn to him. Mio soon leaves for the mainland, but their unexpected connection isn't over. It's a tender, beautifully drawn read for fans of slow, sincere romance and the anime film adaptation.
240: Dungeon Friends Forever by Yasuhisa Kuma (Seven Seas) is a sweet fantasy romantic comedy. Every month, young warrior Van Sirius fights his way through the Wyrm Hole dungeon just to visit its boss, Ryuka Obsidian, a dragon who also happens to be his childhood friend. Her four loyal lieutenants know all about the pair and are desperate to nudge their friendship into something more. It's a cozy, funny read for fans of monster-girl comedies and slow-burn childhood-friend romance.
241: You Call That Service by Kisetsu Morita (Yen Press) is an absurd, offbeat comedy light novel from the author of I've Been Killing Slimes for 300 Years. Ryouta has been dogged by bad luck ever since his grandfather cursed him, so he heads into the mountains hoping to be left alone. Instead he finds Akinomiya, a strange town ruled by vampires, where a proud and eccentric girl named Shiren Fuyukura decides he'll be her servant. It's a goofy, quick read for fans of deadpan humor and oddball supernatural comedy.
242: Yu-Gi-Oh! Arc V by Shin Yoshida and Naohito Miyoshi (Viz Media) is a fast-paced card-battle adventure. In Maiami City, where Leo Corporation's Solid Vision technology has made dueling part of everyday life, Yuya Sakaki is on the run after hacking Leo Corp's system as the mysterious duelist Phantom. When Yuzu Hiiragi offers to help him, the price is signing on as a teacher at her father's dueling school. It's a high-energy read for Yu-Gi-Oh! fans and anyone who loves flashy, strategic duels.
243: Shinobi Life by Shoko Conami (Tokyopop) is a time-crossed romance with ninja action. Lonely rich girl Beni Kujo's world turns upside down when Kagetora, a ninja from the distant past, suddenly drops into her life. He's convinced she's the princess he swore to protect, and he isn't about to leave her side. It's a dramatic, swoony read for fans of bodyguard romances, historical fantasy, and stories where two very different worlds collide.
244: Kaijin Fugeki Kindled Spirits by Oh! Great (Kodansha) is a moody supernatural action story from the creator of Air Gear and Tenjo Tenge. In a world reshaped by mysterious, destructive phenomena called the Night, young Jin lives in a quiet countryside town. There he crosses paths with Gao, a British brigadier general who fled to Japan after a Night took his mother, and whose arrival has tangled their lives together. It's a striking, beautifully drawn read for fans of big, strange battles and slow-burning mysteries.
245: The Antique Gift Shop by Lee Eun (Ice Kunion) is an eerie, folklore-tinged supernatural mystery manhwa. Former college student Bun-nyuh Cho is tricked by her grandmother into running an antique shop, and she bets she can sell every item in the store to win her freedom. If she loses, she'll have to become a shaman like her grandmother. The trouble is that these antiques are cursed, choose their own owners, and change their lives. It's an atmospheric read for fans of Korean folklore and episodic ghost stories.
246: The Condemned Villainess Goes Back In Time by Bakufu Narayama (Seven Seas) is a dark, satisfying revenge fantasy with art by Rat Kitaguni. Claudia, a duke's daughter, is framed by her half-sister, stripped of her engagement, and cast out into a hard life, only to die of illness. She then wakes up at fourteen with all her memories intact and vows to become the ultimate villain to get her revenge. It's a sharp, scheming read for fans of time-loop villainess stories with real bite.
247: As A Reincarnated Aristocrat, I'll Use My Appraisal Skill to Rise in the World by Miraijin A (Kodansha) is a strategic fantasy light novel. Ars Louvent is the young heir of a minor noble house and, secretly, a reincarnated Japanese office worker. He's only average with a sword or in battle plans, but his Appraisal skill lets him see the true talents of the people around him, and he sets out to recruit an exceptional team of followers. It's a satisfying read for fans of kingdom-building and war stories.
248: I Get The Feeling That Nobukuni-San Likes Me by Kosuke Yasuda (Seven Seas) is a sweet, funny high school romantic comedy. Nodoka Nobukuni has never been interested in dating, until Sasaki, a transfer student from Tokyo, arrives in class. Completely inexperienced in romance, she starts following the advice of a self-styled relationship guru and sets out to make him fall for her. It's a charming, low-stakes read for fans of awkward first love and earnest, oddball heroines.
249: Magical Angel Creamy Mami by Emi Mitsuki (Seven Seas) is a playful showbiz comedy spun off from the classic magical-girl anime. Idol Megumi Ayase is used to being on top, until Mami, a magical idol with a starlit glow, joins her agency and steals the spotlight. Consumed by jealousy, Megumi is determined to reclaim her place, even as she can't quite stop looking out for her new junior. It's a fun, nostalgic read for fans of retro magical girls and idol rivalries.
251: Snow and Ink by Miyuki Unohana (Kodansha) is a quiet, wintry dark fantasy romance. Neneo has been sentenced to death for slaughtering his entire village and has nearly accepted his fate when Freya, a withdrawn and wealthy heiress, mysteriously buys his freedom. An outcast herself, she asks him to travel with her into exile in the far north. As the two make their way through deep snow, they slowly find warmth in each other. It's a hushed, beautifully drawn read for fans of melancholy, slow-burn stories.
252: Our Not So Lonely Planet Travel Guide by Mone Sorai (Tokyopop) is a gentle yuri romance and travelogue. Serious Asahi Suzumura and laid-back Mitsuki Sayama agree to travel the world together, with plans to marry when they return to Japan. Country by country, they explore new cultures and cuisines and learn as much about each other, and themselves, as about the places they visit. It's a warm, relaxing read for fans of slice-of-life romance, food, and armchair travel.
253: Midnight Secretary by Tomu Ohmi (Viz Media) is a sultry office romance with a supernatural twist. Kaya Satozuka is a capable, no-nonsense secretary assigned to Kyohei Tohma, the demanding and difficult director of a major company. She soon discovers that her new boss is a vampire, and that keeping his secret is now part of her job. It's a steamy, dramatic read for older shojo fans who enjoy workplace romance and brooding vampire leads.
255: Immortal Hounds by Ryo Yasohachi (Vertical) is a dark, thoughtful seinen crime thriller. In an alternate world where people are instantly resurrected after death, a rare few known as Vectors carry a syndrome that can take that gift away. Detective Shinichi Kenzaki lost his sister after she fell in love with a Vector, and his work soon puts him on the trail of Rin Kazama, a mysterious, highly trained Vector known as the Escape Artist. It's a gripping read for fans of moody police drama and ethical sci-fi.
256: Super Psychic Policeman Chojo by Shun Numa (Viz Media) is a goofy, irreverent police comedy. Most psychic investigators would never use their powers to lie, cheat, and get ahead, but Meguru Chojo isn't most investigators. Stuck at a run-down neighborhood station where the locals can't stand him, he drags his earnest rookie partner, Nao Ippongi, into one ridiculous scheme after another. It's a quick, laugh-out-loud read for fans of gag manga and lovable rogues with very flexible morals.
258: Loving Moon Dog by Nanpei Yamada (Seven Seas) is a sweet, playful supernatural romance. Rikka is a twenty-five-year-old dog groomer with a soft spot for animals, so when she finds an abandoned Doberman, she takes him in. Then her new companion transforms into a handsome man and asks her to be his lover. It's a warm, funny read for fans of devoted love interests, unusual pairings, and romantic comedy with a fairy-tale twist.
259: The Dangerous Convenience Store by 945 (Seven Seas) is a sweet and spicy boys' love manhwa. College student Yeo Euijoon works night shifts at a convenience store in a rough neighborhood to cover his bills, his tuition, and his comatose brother's hospital costs. He stays cheerful despite the gangsters who cause trouble there, and soon a tall, reserved, well-dressed regular, Beom Geonwoo, catches his eye. It's an engaging read for mature BL fans who enjoy slow-building romance with an edge.
260: Twilight Out of Focus by Jyanome (Kodansha) is a tender, funny high school boys' love romance. Second-year students Mao Tsuchiya and Hisashi Otomo share a dorm room under a strict set of roommate rules. When their school's film club decides to shoot a BL short film, Otomo is cast as the lead, while Mao, the cameraman, finds his own feelings getting in the way of the shoot. It's a sweet, heartfelt read for fans of campus romance and the anime adaptation.
261: Modern Villainess Light Novel by Tofuro Futsukaichi (Seven Seas) is a clever financial fantasy with a villainess twist. An office worker laid off after the 2008 financial crisis dies and is reborn as Runa Keikain, the villainess of an otome game who is destined to lose everything in that same crash. Armed with fifteen years of hindsight about money and markets, she sets out to save herself, and maybe Japan's economy, with her loyal butler acting on her behalf. It's a sharp, unusual read for fans of business strategy.
262: In The Name of the Mermaid Princess by Yoshino Fumikawa (Viz Media) is a thoughtful fairy-tale fantasy with art by Miya Tashiro. In the kingdom of Blognig, anyone born with animal traits or special powers is persecuted as an "unhuman," so mermaid princess Mio is kept confined to the palace while doctors try to remove her fins and scales before an arranged marriage. Then a tutor named Yuri tells her she shouldn't have to hide any part of herself. It's an emotional read for fans of reimagined fairy tales.
263: Alpi The Soul Sender by Rona (Titan Manga) is a gentle fantasy journey with a darker undercurrent. In a magical world, divine spirits sustain all life and protect the communities around them, but when they die a curse can turn them malevolent. Soul Senders like Alpi, a gifted young girl traveling with her caring familiar Perenai, guide these spirits to the afterlife. It's a warm, beautifully drawn read for fans of magical girls, quiet adventure, and stories that carry real emotional weight.
265: Tsugumi Project by Ippatu (Kodansha) is a striking post-apocalyptic sci-fi action story. More than two hundred years after a nuclear war, Japan is cut off from the world and overrun by irradiated, mutated monsters. Leon, a French soldier of fortune framed on a false charge, is sent there with other convicts and given one year to recover a powerful lost weapon code-named Tsugumi. When the mission turns deadly, he's saved by a taloned, half-human girl. It's a gorgeous, gritty read for fans of creature-filled wastelands.
266: Easygoing Territory Defense by the Optimistic Lord Light Novel by Sou Akaike (Seven Seas) is a relaxed, upbeat kingdom-building fantasy. Van, a boy reincarnated from Earth as a marquis's youngest son, is born with production magic instead of the elemental magic his family prizes. His disappointed father exiles him to a nearly abandoned village, where Van becomes lord and starts building it up into something remarkable. It's a cozy, satisfying read for fans of town-building isekai and clever, good-natured heroes.
267: My Unique Skill Makes Me Op Light Novel by Nazuna Miki (Kodansha) is a breezy fantasy adventure light novel. Overworked office worker Ryota Sato dies of exhaustion and wakes up in a world with RPG-like rules, where monsters drop the items everyone needs to live. He's stuck at Level 1 forever, but a maxed-out unique skill lets him get extremely rare drops that more than make up for it. It's a light, feel-good read for fans of game-system isekai and the anime adaptation.
268: Diary of a Female Lead: Shujinkou Nikki by Yuu Yoshinaga (Seven Seas) is a sweet, funny shojo romantic comedy. Shy Aoi Tsujimura sees herself as a background character: her older brother Itsuki is a star athlete, her mother is a famous shojo manga artist, and Aoi just wants one true friend. When Itsuki brings home her classmate Sena Mizusawa, the two decide to teach her about romance using shojo manga as their guide. It's a charming read for fans of self-aware, cozy school romance.
270: IDOL x IDOL STORY! by Shotaro Tokuno (Seven Seas) is a heartfelt idol drama from the creator of New Game!. Mimi Nagisa's idol group flopped, and now she's working part-time at a convenience store, where she's mortified to run into Ibuki Nanakusa, a fellow former idol who once admired her. When a big audition for a new group is announced, Ibuki convinces Mimi to give her dream one more shot. It's a warm, encouraging read for fans of idol stories, second chances, and supportive friendships.
271: It Takes More Than a Pretty Face to Fall in Love by Karin Anzai (Seven Seas) is a bubbly shojo romantic comedy. Kanato Ugo is a popular social media influencer, but his grades are so bad that he's close to being expelled. When Sana, a junior who happens to be one of his fans, learns about his situation, she offers to take over his social media so he can focus on studying. It's a light, funny read for fans of school romance and pairings that grow out of unlikely teamwork.
272: Only I Know the World Is Ending by Shigeru Haijima, Tsubasa, and Ryuta Fuse (Seven Seas) is a gritty monster-apocalypse action fantasy. Ordinary office worker Akira Ichijo is killed by a Minotaur on his way home, only to wake up back at his office as monsters invade the real world. His secret Resurrection skill brings him back after every death with his levels and abilities intact, so he fights to survive alongside his childhood friend Nao Nanase. It's a brutal, fast read for fans of time-loop survival stories.
274: My Dear Detective: Mitsuko's Case Files by Natsumi Ito (Seven Seas) is a stylish historical mystery. In 1930s Japan, Mitsuko Hoshino is determined to make it as a detective in a society that looks down on working women. When a waiter named Saku Yoshida brings her first solo case, the two solve it together, and she's impressed enough to hire him as her assistant. It's an elegant, engaging read for fans of period detective stories, sharp heroines, and slow-building partnerships.
277: My Secretly Hot Husband by Harara and Jungyeon (Ize Press) is a cozy fantasy romance manhwa. Reborn into a fantasy world, Letitia is orphaned as a toddler and taken in by a wealthy uncle who treats her like a maid while eyeing her inheritance. Rather than sacrifice one of his own daughters to repay a debt, he sends twelve-year-old Letitia as a bride to Erden, the feared Monster Lord. To her surprise, Erden turns out to be gentle and kind. It's a warm, charming read for fans of found-family stories.
278: The Too-Perfect Saint Light Novel by Fuyutsuki Koki (Seven Seas) is a gentle fantasy romance with a satisfying twist. Philia is the hardworking Saint of her kingdom, engaged to the second prince, until he decides she's too perfect to be lovable and sells her off to a neighboring kingdom that has just lost its own Saint. In her new home, Philia slowly discovers she's been working herself far too hard and that people might actually appreciate her. It's a comforting read for fans of the anime and kind-hearted heroines.
280: Always a Catch! by Mayo Momoyo (Square Enix Manga) is a lively fantasy romantic comedy with art by Kaki Nagato, adapted from the light novel illustrated by Itsuki Mito. Maria Annovazzi, a duke's fifth daughter, loses her place as heir to the family dukedom and heads to the neighboring Kingdom of Rubini to find a husband. She ends up landing far bigger game than expected: the crown prince himself. It's a breezy, funny read for fans of capable heroines and royal romance.
281: Dragon and Chameleon by Ryo Ishiyama (Square Enix Manga) is a sharp, funny body-swap comedy about making manga. Famous artist Garyo Hanagami tries to save his gloomy assistant, Shinobu Miyama, from a fall down the stairs, and the two wake up in each other's bodies. Now Miyama is drawing Hanagami's hit series, while Hanagami, stuck as an unknown, starts a brand-new manga to compete with his own work. It's a clever, energetic read for fans of Bakuman and stories about creative rivalry.
282: Nakamura-san, the Uninvited Gyaru by Sachiko Orihara (Seven Seas) is a light, easygoing romantic comedy. Teppei Akiyama is a twenty-year-old otaku who works at a bar and gets flustered at the drop of a hat. After a rough day, he's nearly hit by a car and is saved by his gyaru coworker, Karin Nakamura, who then asks if she can move into his apartment. It's a sweet, funny read for fans of unexpected roommates, opposites-attract pairings, and slice-of-life romance.
283: Magical Buffs: The Support Caster is Stronger Than He Realized! by Haka Tokura, Shin Arakawa, and Eiri Shirai (Seven Seas) is an upbeat fantasy action story. Support mage Wim Strauss is kicked out of his adventuring party because his teammates think he's useless in battle. Then his childhood friend Heidemarie invites him to join her party instead, giving him a second chance to show what his magic can really do. It's a satisfying, feel-good read for fans of underdog adventurers and party-exile fantasy.
284: Omega Megaera by Maki Marukido (Kodansha) is a sharp, scheming boys' love drama set in an omegaverse world where alphas hold power and omegas are oppressed. Saimon, an omega who married into the powerful Hanabusa family, is shunned as a bringer of misfortune after failing to give his alpha husband an heir. Sent to find the patriarch's illegitimate son, he discovers Mamiya, a street kid secretly an omega, and hatches a daring plan to pass him off as an alpha heir. It's a gripping read for fans of power plays.
285: Blank by Pop Mhan (Tokyopop) is a playful action comedy with a dash of romance from an American comics artist. Aki Clark is a high school girl who trains in martial arts and lives alone while her father works overseas. Her quiet routine is upended by Blank, a teenage boy with amnesia who remembers only two things: he's a secret agent, and his job is to protect her. It's a light, goofy read for fans of bodyguard comedies and manga-style action.
286: Yan by Chang Sheng (Titan Manga) is a dark, stylish revenge thriller from Taiwan. In a harsh near-future world, Yan Tieh-hua was declared dead a decade ago after being imprisoned for a family massacre she didn't commit. Now she's back, and she wants vengeance. The story blends sci-fi, noir, action, and mystery with striking, dynamic artwork. It's a gripping read for fans of hard-edged crime stories, morally gray heroines, and cinematic action.
287: Formerly, The Fallen Daughter of the Duke by Saki Ichibu (Tokyopop) is a fantasy romance with a villainess twist, illustrated by Ushio Shirotori. Claire Martino had a loving family, an engagement to the crown prince, and a bright future built on her family's inherited magic, until her own half-sister took it all away in an instant. Branded a villain and the daughter of a disgraced duke, Claire leaves home to discover who she really is. It's an engaging read for fans of otome-game-style fantasy and resilient heroines.
288: Galaxy Angel by Kanan (Broccoli Books) is a bright, playful space-opera comedy based on the popular game and anime franchise. The Angel Troupe is an elite squad of young women who pilot powerful Emblem Frame starships in defense of the Transbaal Empire. Between battles, though, their personalities clash as often as their ships do, and missions rarely go as planned. It's a cheerful, colorful read for fans of the anime, sci-fi action with a light touch, and ensemble casts full of big personalities.
289: Tamamo-chan's A Fox by Ray Yuki (Seven Seas) is a sweet, fluffy supernatural school comedy. Tamamo, a fox from Kyoto's Inari Shrine who might just be a goddess, transforms into a human girl so she can experience high school. Her transformation doesn't quite work, leaving her adorably furry, but the adults don't notice and her classmates treat her like any other girl. It's a gentle, charming read for fans of cute animal spirits, slice-of-life school comedy, and low-stakes everyday fun.
291: Ghost Talkers Daydream by Saki Okuse (Dark Horse) is a dark, risque supernatural drama with art by Sankichi Meguro. Misaki Saiki can see and speak with the dead, a gift she uses as a medium helping lingering spirits move on. To pay the bills, she also works as a dominatrix, which makes for a very unusual double life. It's an edgy, atmospheric read for mature readers who enjoy moody horror, troubled spirits, and unconventional heroines.
292: Ten Count by Rihito Takarai (Sublime) is an intense, emotional boys' love drama for mature readers. Tadaomi Shirotani, a company secretary, suffers from severe mysophobia that makes everyday life a struggle. A chance meeting with Riku Kurose, a counselor, leads to an unusual proposal: work through a list of ten steps to overcome his compulsions. As the steps progress, their relationship grows into something more complicated. It's a striking, beautifully drawn read for fans of slow-burn psychological romance.
293: Apocalypse Zero by Takayuki Yamaguchi (Media Blasters) is an over-the-top, ultra-violent shonen action horror story. In a Tokyo left in ruins after a devastating earthquake, brothers Kakugo and Harara Hagakure are trained by their father to hunt the monsters that roam the city, wearing powerful armored exoskeletons built by their grandfather. When Harara falls under an evil force and turns against humanity, Kakugo must fight to stop him. It's a wild, grotesque read for mature fans of extreme action and cult classic manga.
294: Aquarian Age Juvenile Orion by Sakurako Gokurakuin (Broccoli Books) is a romantic shojo fantasy based on the Aquarian Age card game. Sixteen-year-old Mana returns to her hometown to reunite with her childhood friend Kaname after seven years apart, only to find he's changed. Her return draws Kaname, his best friend Naoya, and several classmates and teachers into the Aquarian Age, a secret war that has raged for thousands of years. It's a dreamy, dramatic read for fans of reincarnation fantasy and bishonen-filled casts.
295: B.B. Explosion by Yasue Imai (Viz Media) is an upbeat showbiz story for younger readers. Airi Ishikawa, a talented girl from Okinawa, enrolls in a performing arts school in the big city with big dreams. She hopes to land a spot on Boom Boom, a weekly variety show that features fresh talent, and maybe meet her idol, a member of the boy band Da Pump. It's a fun, energetic read for fans of dance, music, and determined heroines chasing their dreams.
296: Bakegyamon by Mitsuhisa Tamura (Viz Media) is a lively monster-battle adventure, based on a story by Kazuhiro Fujita. Sanshiro is an ordinary boy who gets pulled into Bakegyamon, a mysterious game where kids team up with monsters and battle each other for the chance to have a wish granted. With his monster partner at his side, he faces off against tough opponents and even tougher creatures. It's a fun, fast-paced read for younger fans of Pokemon-style battles and spooky yokai.
298: Heavenly Executioner Chiwoo by Park KangHo and Lee HaNa (Ice Kunion) is a sweeping historical fantasy action manhwa. Young Chiwoo discovers that his father was a mangnani, one of ancient Korea's executioners, just as an emperor's army sets out to wipe them out. When soldiers attack his uncle, Chiwoo takes up the role of mangnani himself. It's an energetic, action-packed read for fans of martial arts, historical adventure, and heroes forced to grow up fast.
299: Hero Tales by Huang Jin Zhou (Yen Press) is a martial-arts fantasy adventure drawn by Hiromu Arakawa of Fullmetal Alchemist. After his coming-of-age ceremony, Taitou receives a legendary sword that only a true hero can draw, but he can't pull it free. When a thief claims Taitou is the avatar of a star destined to plunge the world into chaos and steals the sword, Taitou sets out with his sister and a wandering priest to get it back. It's a fun read for fans of Arakawa and kung fu adventure.
300: Night of the Beasts by Chika Shiomi (Go! Comi) is a dark supernatural romance with plenty of bite. Aria is a tough high school girl known for standing up to her school's worst bullies, but she finds herself drawn to Sakura, a boy possessed by a demon who could turn violent at any moment, and who insists that Aria is the one who can save him. It's a moody, intense read for fans of brooding shojo with a dangerous edge.
301: Baron Gong Battle by Masayuki Taguchi (Anime Works) is a gritty sci-fi action series built around one relentless fight. Baron Gong is locked in a war with the Neo-Humes, the surviving products of Nazi biological experiments. They are powerful, nearly unkillable, and every one of them wants the Baron dead. It's violent and pulpy, a good fit for readers who like over-the-top battles and a grim, mature tone.
302: The Key to the Kingdom by Kyoko Shitou (CMX) is a classic fantasy adventure about a reluctant heir. After 300 years of war between three rival kingdoms,  the king of Landor and his heroic elder son die in battle, and gentle Prince Astarion, who would rather end the war than fight it, is left to rule, unless someone finds the legendary Key to the Kingdom first. It's a warm, old-fashioned quest for fans of court intrigue.
303: The King of Fighters: A New Beginning by Kyotaro Azuma (Seven Seas) is a fast, punchy tournament manga based on SNK's fighting game The King of Fighters XIV. Fighters from around the world gather for a new King of Fighters tournament hosted by the mysterious Antonov. Veteran martial artist Tung Fu Rue guides his students as the matches grow tougher. It's a fun read for fans of the games and anyone who enjoys big fights and a large, colorful cast.
304: The Lady Knight and the Beast-Eared Child by Taboengine (Seven Seas) is a gentle fantasy about two lonely people who find each other. Olivia is a solitary monster hunter who never wanted company, but after she rescues Noah, a young Beastkin boy, she reluctantly takes him on as her apprentice. She teaches him how to fight, and he teaches her to notice the quiet, good moments in a harsh world. It's a cozy, heartfelt pick for fans of found-family stories.
305: NTR: Netsuzou Trap by Naoko Kodama (Seven Seas) is a yuri drama about a friendship that crosses a line. Yuma has just started dating her first boyfriend, so she turns to her confident childhood friend Hotaru for advice. Hotaru offers to help her "practice," and their secret closeness quickly becomes something neither of them can easily explain away. It's a tense, messy romance for readers who like complicated relationships and plenty of emotional tension.
306: The Princess of Convenient Plot Devices by Mamecyoro (Yen Press), with art by Kazusa Yoneda, is a lighthearted fantasy romance. Maki wakes up inside her favorite boys' love novel as Princess Octavia, sister of the very prince she loves to see paired with his partner. The problem is that the couple expects Octavia to supply the royal heir, but she refuses a loveless political match and resolves to find a man worth falling for. It's a playful read for fans of isekai and romantic comedy.
308: I Can't Say No to the Lonely Girl by Kashikaze (Kodansha) is a yuri romantic comedy about a deal that turns into something more. Ayaka Sakurai is a hardworking class representative who badly needs a teacher's recommendation. To get it, she has to bring chronically absent Sora Honda back to school, and Sora agrees, but only if Ayaka grants her a request every day. It's a sweet, slow-burn story for readers who enjoy two very different girls growing closer.
310: Our Kingdom by Naduki Koujima (June) is a boys' love family drama about an unexpected inheritance. After his grandmother dies, orphaned Akira Nonaka is taken in by his wealthy relatives, the Takatou family, and suddenly finds himself competing with his cousin Rei to become the family's next head. As the rivalry pulls them closer, Akira has to face feelings he never expected. It's a soapy, character-driven story for fans of rich-family intrigue and slow-building romance.
311: Oyayubihime Infinity by Toru Fujieda (CMX) is a gentle shojo romance about destiny and second chances. Tsubame is searching for his soul mate, Agemaki, the girl he believes he was meant to find. When he meets Kanoko, who has a butterfly-shaped birthmark on her hand, he's sure she's the one, and soon they meet other teens with matching marks and stories of their own. It's a sweet, bittersweet read for fans of fated-love tales with a touch of the fairy tale.
312: I'm a Wolf, but My Boss Is a Sheep! by Shino Shimizu (Seven Seas) is a cozy office romantic comedy with fluffy charm. Oogami is a wolf-man working at a bedding company where nearly all of his coworkers are sheep, and he prefers to keep his head down, but his new department comes with a supervisor he can't stop thinking about. It's a light, adorable read for fans of workplace romance and animal-people stories.
313: I.N.V.U. by Kang Won Kim (Tokyopop) is a lively Korean teen romance with a big, quirky cast. Sixteen-year-old Sey Hong is shy and wary of boys, and when her novelist mother leaves for Italy, Sey is left with the Kang family, near-strangers with secrets of their own; between her scheming friends and Siho, a gas-station owner with a complicated home life, her quiet life gets messy fast. It's a fun, soapy pick for fans of school romance and ensemble drama.
314: Blue Sheep Reverie by Makoto Tateno (June) is a moody boys' love crime drama set in a gang-ruled city. When Kai's lover Maria is murdered, his only clue is the missing ring she always wore, a man-made blue jewel. He spots it on the hand of Lahti, a powerful leader in one of the gangs that run the city of Akatsuki, and to get closer to the truth, Kai becomes Lahti's bodyguard. It's a stylish, tense read for fans of dark romance and underworld intrigue.
315: The Summer You Were There by Yuama (Seven Seas) is a tender yuri romance with a bittersweet glow. Shizuku Hoshikawa is a quiet high school loner who secretly writes novels. When her popular classmate Kaori Asaka reads her work, she loves it and asks Shizuku to write a romance about the two of them, and when Shizuku refuses, Kaori asks her out on a date instead. It's a gentle, emotional story for readers who enjoy quiet, heartfelt romance.
316: Bring It On! by Hyekyung Baek (Ice Kunion) is a scrappy Korean romantic comedy with a fighting heroine. Miha is a fiercely competitive tomboy who hates losing, and years of tough training from her brother have made her the terror of every boy around her, until a confident, good-looking transfer student named Sung-suh arrives and decides he's going to win her over. It's a fun, high-energy read for fans of battling-couples romance.
317: Though You May Burn to Ash by Kakashi Oniyazu (Yen Press) is a seinen death-game thriller with a strange twist. High schooler Ryouma Shinomiya desperately needs a billion yen to pay for his sister's medical care. After accepting a mysterious woman's invitation to play a game, he dies in an accident and wakes up in a girl's body alongside other players, where winning means a fortune and losing means death. It's a tense, mature pick for fans of survival games.
318: Island by In-wan Youn and Kyung-il Yang (Tokyopop) is a dark Korean horror-action series steeped in folklore. Mi-Ban, a young woman from a wealthy family, travels to a remote island off the Korean coast to teach. There she is drawn into a world of demons and spirits, and her only protection is Ban, a mysterious and violent half-demon. It's a bloody, atmospheric read for fans of supernatural horror and brooding antiheroes.
319: Cheerful Amnesia by Tamamushi Oku (Yen Press) is a sweet yuri romantic comedy with a light touch. Arisa Suzuki wakes up in the hospital missing the last three years of her life, including her relationship with her girlfriend, Mari. Instead of a tearful struggle to remember, Arisa simply falls head over heels for Mari all over again. It's a warm, silly, affectionate read for anyone who wants an easygoing couple story.
320: Togainu no Chi by Suguro Chayamachi (Tokyopop) is a gritty boys' love action story set in a ruined, lawless city. After a devastating war, Akira is offered a deal: fight in Igura, a deadly underground battle game in the city of Toshima, and his murder charge will be dropped. Once inside, he finds a violent world ruled by a mysterious figure called Il-Re. Based on the visual novel, it's a dark, intense pick for fans of tough antiheroes and survival stories.
323: Cocoon Entwined by Yuriko Hara (Yen Press) is an elegant, slightly eerie yuri drama set at an elite girls' school. The school is known for its uniforms, which are woven from the hair of its own students, and among its girls, admiration, longing, and quiet obsession knot together into a love triangle that only one of them fully understands. It's a haunting, beautifully drawn pick for fans of classic girls'-school romance with a darker edge.
324: Totally Captivated by Hajin Yoo (Netcomics) is a Korean boys' love drama with a dangerous edge. Ewon is a poor but brilliant university student who gets forced into running risky errands for a loan shark, thanks to his bitter ex-boyfriend, Jiho. The gang's leader, Mookyul, takes a keen interest in his new errand boy, and the two soon learn their history runs deeper than either realized. It's a dramatic, emotional read for fans of gangster romance.
325: Kamunagara: Rebirth of the Demonslayer by Hajime Yamamura (Anime Works) is a supernatural action series rooted in Japanese myth. Hitaka Kugaya, a former kendo champion, is warned by a classmate that a storm is coming. He soon learns he is the reincarnation of a legendary hero, and that demons from another world are breaking through the seal between the worlds. It's a moody, sword-swinging pick for fans of reincarnation stories and demon-hunting action.
326: Coffee Moon by Mochito Bota (Yen Press) is a quiet, mysterious fantasy with a melancholy mood. Pieta is an ordinary girl living in a world where black rain never stops falling, and she takes comfort in her routine, especially her daily walk to school and her chats with her friend Danae. Then one day that familiar conversation doesn't happen, and her everyday life starts to come apart. It's a dreamy, atmospheric read for fans of gentle, puzzling stories.
329: Kingdom of Z by Saizo Harawata and Ron Watanuki (Seven Seas) is a zombie survival story with a sharp, unpredictable edge. Five days after an outbreak begins, Masaru is barely hanging on, hiding out at his high school. He's rescued by two high school girls, Miki Sekigahara and Karin Nagiri, but it's not clear what his rescuers really want. It's a tense, gory read for fans of zombie action and survival thrillers.
330: Recast by Seung-Hui Kye (Tokyopop) is a Korean fantasy action series set in a layered world of gods, humans, and demons. JD is a Recast, a being created from the life force of his grandfather, Grifford, once an immortal and powerful magician. JD carries a weapon that can become anything he imagines, which comes in handy, because bounty hunters are always on his trail. It's a fast, fun pick for fans of quirky fantasy adventure.
332: Reincarnated as a Sword: Another Wish by Yuu Tanaka and Hinako Inoue (Seven Seas) is a fantasy action spin-off with a lot of heart. A man wakes up in another world reborn as a sentient magic sword, with his memories but not his name. He rescues Fran, a young cat-eared girl, from slavery, and together they set out on new adventures as she grows stronger. It's a lively pick for fans of the original series and anyone who enjoys a devoted partner duo.
336: Demon Sacred by Natsumi Itsuki (Tokyopop) is an offbeat shojo sci-fi fantasy about demons who take on human faces. Scientist Shinobu cares for twin sisters Mona and Rina, and Rina has "return syndrome," a condition that makes people slowly disappear. A demon named Mika offers a way to save her, at a cost. It's a strange, imaginative read for fans of unusual shojo.
337: When I Became a Commoner, They Broke Off Our Engagement! by Kenzi Oiwa (Yen Press), with art by Kaoru Takanashi, is a gentle fantasy about starting over. Anna grew up in a noble family but looked nothing like them and had no talent for their magic, because a mischievous fairy swapped her at birth, and once the truth comes out, she's disowned and her engagement is called off, leaving her to adjust to life with her new commoner family. It's a warm, hopeful read for fans of fresh-start stories.
338: Laon by YoungBin Kim (Yen Press), with art by Hyun You, is a playful Korean fantasy drawn from folklore. When the police find a naked, hungry boy wandering the street, they have no idea what to do with him, because he's actually a nine-tailed fox, or he would be, if he hadn't lost his tails in a bet, and now he has to win them back before other spirits get to them. It's a lively, funny read for fans of mythological mischief.
339: Last Fantasy by Creative Hon and Yong-Wan Kwon (Tokyopop) is a slapstick Korean fantasy comedy that pokes fun at classic RPGs. Tian is a powerful but untrained sorcerer, and his best friend Drei von Richenstein is a walking disaster who can ruin any quest, whether by drinking healing potions when he's thirsty or picking fights with friendly dragons. It's a goofy, fast-paced read for gamers and anyone who enjoys a good fantasy parody.
340: Last Round Arthurs by Taro Hitsuji (Yen Press), with illustrations by Kiyotaka Haimura, is a fantasy action light novel that drops the legend of King Arthur into a modern school. A battle to choose the next King Arthur is underway, and the candidates fight with Knights of the Round Table at their sides. Luna Artur, the weakest contender, recruits Rintarou Magami, a gifted and mysterious boy, as her vassal. It's an energetic pick for fans of magic-battle stories and Arthurian twists.
342: Devilman Grimoire by Go Nagai and Rui Takato (Seven Seas) is a horror action reimagining of the classic Devilman. A teenage boy is possessed by a demon and becomes Devilman, turning that terrible power against the hellspawn invading the human world. It's violent, dark, and stylish, with plenty of monster battles. It's a good pick for longtime Devilman fans and newcomers who like their action with a horror edge.
343: Dogsred by Satoru Noda (Viz Media), the creator of Golden Kamuy, is a hard-hitting sports manga set on the ice. Rou is a former figure skater looking for a second chance, and he finds it in the rough-and-tumble world of ice hockey. Noda brings the same energy and eye for detail that made his earlier work a hit. It's a great pick for sports-manga fans and anyone curious about a sport that rarely gets the manga treatment.
344: Love Attack! by Shizuru Seino (Tokyopop) is a bright, funny shojo romantic comedy. Chiemi Yusa is a first-year high schooler who keeps getting into fights defending bullied classmates. Her teacher threatens to expel her unless she can reform Akifumi Hirata, a feared student known as the "Deranged Devil," and after a dramatic first meeting Chiemi agrees to date him and finds he's kinder than his reputation. It's a sweet, lighthearted read for fans of tough-girl romance.
346: You're So Cool by YoungHee Lee (Yen Press) is a Korean romantic comedy with a soft heart under the jokes. Clumsy, cheerful Nan Woo has had a crush on Seung Ha, her school's perfect top student, for ages. When they finally start dating, she discovers that he lives a very different life after school, hiding old hurts behind a cool mask. It's a funny, sincere read for fans of school romance with emotional depth.
347: Eden of Witches by Yumeji (Kana) is a lush, gentle fantasy about nature and those who can hear it. Humans have stripped the world nearly bare, and the witches, who can speak with plants and animals, are blamed and forced into hiding. Young witch apprentice Pili sets out with her wolf companion, Oak, but after a bad fall she is taken in by a village boy named Bowei, in a place where witches are hunted. It's a beautiful, heartfelt pick for fans of Studio Ghibli-style adventure.
348: Even Dogs Go to Other Worlds by Ryuuou and Hana Ichika (Seven Seas) is a cozy isekai comedy about a man and his best friend. Takumi is an overworked office worker whose only comfort is his little Maltese, Leo. One day he's transported to another world and wakes up next to a giant wolf, and that wolf turns out to be Leo, transformed into a mighty fenrir. It's a warm, easygoing read for dog lovers and fans of laid-back fantasy.
349: Failed Princesses by Ajiichi (Seven Seas) is a yuri romantic comedy about two girls who never should have crossed paths. Nanaki Fujishiro and Kaede Kurokawa run in completely different social circles at school. When they're thrown together, an unlikely friendship begins, and they slowly start working out what they mean to each other. It's a warm, funny, and heartfelt read for fans of opposites-attract school stories.
350: Shiki Tsukai by To-Ru Zekuu and Yuna Takanagi (Del Rey) is a shonen fantasy action series built around the power of the seasons. Just before his fourteenth birthday, Akira Kizuki learns he is a shiki tsukai, a warrior who can command the seasons, and a rare one who can wield all four at once. Koyomi, a girl who can transform into a sword, becomes his protector as a hidden war over the balance of nature heats up. It's a fun pick for fans of elemental battles.
351: SINoALICE by Takuto Aoki and Himiko (Square Enix), based on Yoko Taro's mobile game, is a dark, violent fantasy that twists familiar fairy tales. High schooler Alice is haunted by strange dreams in which two marionettes ask her what she wants, until she wakes to find her family murdered and a calm stranger sitting in her kitchen, pulled into a death game where every player has magical powers. It's an intense, gory pick for mature readers who like their stories strange and grim.
352: Delinquent Daddy and Tender Teacher by Tama Mizuki (Seven Seas) is a sweet boys' love story about family and first love. Hitsuji, a gentle elementary school teacher, never confessed his high school crush on his friend Hatoyama, a good-natured former delinquent. Years later, Hitsuji discovers Hatoyama is raising his son alone and starts helping him learn to cook and keep house, old feelings return. It's a heartwarming read for fans of cozy, domestic romance.
353: Slow Life in Another World (I Wish!) by Shinkoshoto (Seven Seas), with manga art by Nagayori, is a laid-back isekai. Itsuki Shimomiya, an exhausted office worker, is reborn in a fantasy world with a skill that gives him a large sum of money once a day. He'd love to relax instead of fighting monsters, but the cost of living there turns out to be steep, so he sets out to build a comfortable life using what he knows from his old world. It's easygoing fun for fans of relaxed fantasy.
355: TenRyu: The Dragon Cycle by Sanami Matoh (CMX) is a sword-swinging fantasy adventure set in war-torn ancient China. Two swordsman brothers set out to find the man who killed their father. Their quest for revenge soon turns into a sprawling adventure, full of weapon-wielding women, determined enemies, and secrets about the brothers' own origins. It's a fun, action-packed pick for fans of martial arts epics and brotherly banter.
360: I Don't Know Which Is Love by Tamamushi Oku (Yen Press) is a yuri romantic comedy about moving on and starting fresh. Mei Soraike finally works up the courage to confess to the best friend she's secretly loved, and gets turned down. Instead of moping, she takes the heartbreak in stride and heads off to college determined to find a girlfriend. It's a light, warm read for fans of college romance and hopeful, upbeat love stories.
361: Cat on the Hero's Lap by Kousuke Iijima and Shiori (Seven Seas) is a goofy fantasy gag comedy with a furry troublemaker at its center. The adventurer Red and his companions, a fighter and a wizard, keep trying to reach the Demon King's lair, but every time, an orange tabby called Mr. Cat climbs into Red's lap, and the quest grinds to a halt. It's a silly, charming read for cat lovers and anyone who enjoys RPG parodies.
362: Disciple of the Lich by Nekoko (Seven Seas), illustrated by Yoh Hihara, is a dark fantasy light novel about surviving at rock bottom. An ordinary teen is transported to another world, accidentally angers the gods, and is dropped into the depths of the world's deepest dungeon with no skills or magic. There he meets an undead girl who dislikes humans but agrees to help him survive. It's a gritty, determined pick for fans of dungeon-crawl isekai.
363: Let Dai by Sooyeon Won (Netcomics) is an intense Korean boys' love drama set in a bleak, gang-ruled Seoul. Jaehee is an honest high school student who steps in to stop a gang from mugging a girl. That act puts him in the path of Dai, the reckless, unpredictable leader of the gang, and pulls him into a relationship full of passion and pain. It's a dark, emotional, and often harrowing read for fans of tragic romance.
365: RaW Hero by Akira Hiramoto (Yen Press) is a raunchy, over-the-top seinen comedy about heroes and villains. Chiaki is an unemployed young man supporting his two brothers. After a misunderstanding with a government agent, he's recruited as a double agent inside SALF, a criminal organization of super-powered villains, and a mishap at the recruiting event lands him in disguise. It's a wild, irreverent read for mature fans of the creator's Prison School.
366: Choking on Love by Keiko Iwashita (Seven Seas) is a romance about a careful planner meeting a free spirit. Hibari is a focused art student who dreams of becoming a graphic designer and worries she's ordinary next to her classmates. After a messy run-in at a ramen shop, carefree guitarist Gaku starts upending her neatly planned life, and she begins to wonder if a little chaos might be good for her. It's a warm read for fans of college romance.
368: Pink Candy Kiss by Ami Uozumi (Viz Media) is a quiet, grown-up romance drama about a feeling that never went away. Twenty years ago, Takara nearly kissed Ema, a girl from her middle school. Now the two reconnect as adults, and Ema is married. It's a tender, bittersweet read for fans of mature queer romance and stories about second chances.
369: The Villainess Stans the Heroes by Yamori Mitikusa and Kaoru Harugano (Yen Press) is a playful fantasy romance with a devoted fan at its heart. A woman is reborn in her favorite game as its villainess and, instead of fighting her fate, decides to play the antagonist perfectly, so that the heroes she adores can grow strong enough to save the world. But a childhood decision has already pulled one of her favorites into her life as her right-hand man. It's a fun pick for fans of villainess stories.
371: Father, I Don't Want This Marriage by Hong Heesu and Roal (Inklore) is a dramatic fantasy romance about a second chance at life. Juvelian, a duke's daughter almost everyone despises, is falsely accused of poisoning the empire's princess and abandoned by her father. Given a fresh start, she sets out to change her ending, but her father's ambitious protégé still sees her as an obstacle, and the feared crown prince is never far away. It's a lush, full-color read for fans of palace intrigue.
373: The Ephemeral Scenes of Setsuna's Journey by Rokusyou and Usuasagi (Yen Press) is a gentle, bittersweet fantasy light novel about life on the road. Summoned to another world as its 68th hero, Setsuna Sugimoto is abandoned because of his frail health. Then Kyle, a former hero, gives him a second chance at life, along with his knowledge and power, and Setsuna sets out as an adventurer, meeting all kinds of people along the way. It's a reflective pick for readers who like quieter fantasy.
374: Golosseum by Yasushi Baba (Kodansha) is a gleefully ridiculous action comedy that turns world politics into a wrestling match. Scientists create a material that makes people immune to every weapon ever invented, but instead of ending war, it turns global conflict into an all-out martial-arts brawl. Now Rasputin and Russia's President Putinov are scheming to control the world's supply, and only a band of muscle-bound heroes can stop them. It's a loud, absurd treat for fans of wrestling and over-the-top parody.
375: Minato's Laundromat by Yuzu Tsubaki and Sawa Kanzume (Yen Press) is a gentle boys' love romantic comedy with a small-town feel. Akira Minato, a man in his thirties, quits his Tokyo office job to take over his grandfather's laundromat back home, where he strikes up an odd friendship with Shintaro, a high school student who keeps turning up at the shop. When Akira lets slip that he's gay, Shintaro starts earnestly pursuing him. It's a sweet, low-key read that also inspired a live-action TV drama.
376: Vampeerz by Akili (Denpa) is a moody, stylish yuri romance with a supernatural twist. A girl named Ichika meets Aria, a vampire, at her grandmother's funeral, and the two begin a relationship that is as tender as it is strange. Akili's art is striking, and the story leans into atmosphere and emotion. It's a good pick for fans of gothic romance and vampire stories that focus on feelings over fights.
370: Therapy Game Restart by Meguru Hinohara (SuBLime) is a boys' love romance about what happens after the happy ending. In this sequel to Therapy Game, Shizuma and Minato are officially a couple, but Shizuma has just started as a resident veterinarian and is so swamped he barely has time for dates, and when he finally makes room for Minato, his spirited partner makes it clear he won't be ignored. It's a warm, grown-up read for fans of the original.
378: Astro Royale by Ken Wakui (Viz Media), the creator of Tokyo Revengers, is a supernatural action story about a family at war with itself. The Yotsurugi family has turned away from its criminal past, but when its leader dies, the choice of successor sparks fury among his many adopted sons. That same night, a meteor shower strikes Tokyo, Hibari Yotsurugi awakens a wish-granting power called Astro, and soon the brothers are fighting over the city. It's a loud, energetic pick for fans of brawling, delinquent-style action.
383: Now That We Draw by Kyu Takahata and Yuwji Kaba (Seven Seas) is a seinen romantic comedy about two aspiring manga artists. High schooler Yuuki Uehara is crushed when an editor rejects his romantic comedy manuscript as unrealistic, then learns his popular gyaru classmate Niina Miyamoto got the exact same feedback. Her solution is a fake relationship, so they can both gain some real-life experience for their manga. It's a fun, sweet read for fans of fake-dating stories and behind-the-scenes looks at making manga.
385: Marriage of Convenience by KEN and Antstudio (Ize Press) is a full-color fantasy romance about fixing a marriage the second time around. Bianca de Arno was known as a proud, spendthrift countess who ignored her husband, but after a lonely death she wakes up at nineteen, back in her castle. Determined not to repeat the poverty of her first life, she sets out to reconcile with the distant husband she once resented, despite years of misunderstandings. It's a satisfying read for fans of second-chance romance.
389: Spring Storm and Monster by Mitsubachi Miyuki (Yen Press) is a shojo romantic comedy about an unexpected new family. Ranko Haruno would rather avoid people entirely, keeping her world limited to her mother and her pet pig. After she runs away from Kaya Amamine, an intimidating classmate, her mother announces she's remarrying, and Ranko's new stepbrother turns out to be Kaya. It's a sweet, funny read for fans of shy heroines and gruff boys with soft hearts.
393: Pink & Habanero by Mika Satonaka (Yen Press) is a bright shojo romantic comedy with a secret at its center. Mugi Miyao is a socially awkward high school girl with zero romantic experience, until she discovers that Kei Kurose, her blunt and popular classmate, has a secret part-time job at a cosplay cafe where the staff dress as knights. Keeping his secret pulls the two into a complicated, charming relationship. It's a fun read for fans of school romance with a sharp-tongued love interest.
395: The War of Greedy Witches by Homura Kawamoto and Makoto Shiozuka (Yen Press) is a dark fantasy battle royale. Joan of Arc is rescued from the stake by demons and brought to the court of a demon queen, where she and 31 other famous women from history are forced into Walpurgis, a tournament of fights to the death where each woman wields magic tied to her deepest desire, and the last one standing gets a wish. It's a stylish, intense read from the writer of Kakegurui.
307: Black Rose Alice by Setona Mizushiro (Viz Media) is a lush, unsettling shojo fantasy with a gothic heart. In early-1900s Vienna, Dimitri, a gifted young tenor, dies and returns as a vampire, in a world where vampires don't bite to reproduce but spread like plants, sowing seeds in a human host, and decades later his story becomes tangled with a young woman's desperate bargain in modern Japan. It's a dark, strange, and beautifully drawn read for fans of romance with real horror in it.
322: Pokemon Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire by Hidenori Kusaka and Satoshi Yamamoto (Viz Media) is a fast, fun kids' adventure based on the hit games. Trainers Ruby and Sapphire face a brand-new threat to the Hoenn region: a giant meteorite on a collision course with the planet. Racing to stop it, they cross paths with legendary Pokemon and new rivals. It's a great pick for young Pokemon fans and anyone who grew up with the games.
328: Vampire Doll: Guilt-Na-Zan by Erika Kari (Tokyopop) is a goofy shojo supernatural comedy with a bratty undead hero. Guilt-na-zan was once a powerful vampire, but he's been sealed away for a very long time. When he's finally brought back, his spirit ends up trapped inside the body of a doll, stuck living with a scheming young priest and his sister. It's a light, silly read for fans of gothic comedy and mismatched household antics.
331: Reiko the Zombie Shop by Rei Mikamoto (Dark Horse) is a gory, darkly funny horror series. Reiko Himezono is a teenage necromancer who brings the dead back to life for a fee, usually so her clients can ask the newly risen who killed them. The reanimated rarely stay calm for long, and things get bloody fast. It's an over-the-top, grisly read for horror fans who like their scares with a wicked sense of humor.
334: Kizuna: Bonds of Love by Kazuma Kodaka (DMP) is a classic boys' love drama with a yakuza edge. Ranmaru Samejima was a promising kendo champion until he was hit by a car meant for Kei Enjouji, his lover and the son of a yakuza boss. His injuries end his kendo career, but not their relationship, and as they try to build a life together, Kei's family ties keep pulling danger into their world. It's an emotional, dramatic read for fans of vintage BL.
358: Animal Crossing: New Horizons Deserted Island Diary by Kokonasu Rumba (Viz Media) is a cheerful gag comedy based on the beloved game. The story follows a newcomer settling into island life alongside a cast of wacky animal neighbors. Short, silly chapters riff on everything fans know from the game, from fishing and bug catching to home loans. It's an easy, funny read for kids and grown-up Animal Crossing fans alike.
359: So I'm a Spider, So What? The Daily Lives of the Kumoko Sisters by Okina Baba (Yen Press), with art by Gratinbird, is a cute comedy spin-off. Instead of the main story's dungeon battles, it follows Kumoko and her many sisters through silly, bite-sized everyday adventures, drawn in an adorable chibi style. It's a light, fun read for fans of the original series and the anime who want more time with its spider heroine.
388: Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World- Short Story Collection by Tappei Nagatsuki (Yen Press) is a set of side stories from the popular fantasy series. Rather than pushing the main plot forward, these tales fill in quieter moments with Subaru, Emilia, Rem, Ram, and the rest of the cast, adding warmth, humor, and extra background. It's a treat for readers who already love the light novels or the anime and want more time with their favorite characters.
390: Ichi the Killer by Hideo Yamamoto (Seven Seas) is a brutal seinen crime thriller and a cult classic. When a yakuza boss vanishes along with a fortune, his masochistic enforcer Kakihara tears through Tokyo's underworld looking for answers. The trail leads to Ichi, a timid, deeply disturbed young man who becomes a terrifying killer in the hands of a manipulative old man. It's extremely violent and unflinching, best suited to mature readers with a strong stomach.
396: Welcome to Demon School! Iruma-kun: IruMafia Edition by Osamu Nishi and hiroja (Vertical) is a stylish alternate take on the hit comedy. In a slum run by the mafia, five-year-old orphan Iruma saves the life of Don Sullivan of the Babel Family, who adopts him as his grandson, and raised among gangsters and trained by the stern Kalego, Iruma rises to become the family's second-in-command by fourteen. It's a grittier, sharply dressed romp for fans of the original series.
397: Nezumi's First Love by Riku Oseto (Vertical) is a seinen crime romance with a dark, tender heart. Nezumi is a young woman raised by the yakuza to be an assassin, and she has never known what it means to love someone until she meets Ao, an ordinary young man, at an arcade's claw machines. As their relationship grows, she has to balance it against her violent work and her past. It's a gripping, bittersweet read for fans of crime stories and unlikely love.
398: Sheltering Eaves by Rie Aruga (Kodansha), the creator of Perfect World, is a gentle josei romance with real-world weight. The love story unfolds within Japan's foster care system, and it honestly portrays the struggles of the children who grow up there. Aruga keeps the romance at the center while treating those difficult realities with care. It's a thoughtful, moving read for fans of grounded, emotional drama.
399: Phantom Busters by Neoshoco (Viz Media) is a lively shonen comedy about ghost hunting at school. On his first day at Ryuoh High in Kamakura, elite student Eugene Korekishi, who flatly refuses to believe in the supernatural, meets Mogari Shishikuno, a trainee exorcist from a long line of spirit mediums. Together they start the Paranormal Research Club, better known as the Phantom Busters, and set out to take on evil spirits. It's a fun, funny read for fans of supernatural buddy stories.
382: If the Villainess and Villain Met and Fell in Love by Harunadon (Yen Press), illustrated by Yomi Sarachi, is a fantasy romance light novel about two misunderstood people. Brigitte Meidell was expected to form a powerful spirit contract, but she bonded with a weak, nameless spirit and became an embarrassment to her noble family, and then the prince publicly breaks off their engagement. The one person who stands by her is Yuri, a duke's son feared for his cold manner. It's a sweet pick for fans of villainess stories.
386: Catalog of Wonders by Chizutokouro (Yen Press), with illustrations by Kei Mochizuki, is a spooky middle-grade novel with a lesson in every story. After a bad test score, Mashiro wishes his parents could just forget it. A girl in an eye patch and pink hoodie appears and shows him a mysterious black catalog full of strange products, like a button that erases memories, and each short story follows a customer who learns that these wishes come with a price. It's a great pick for young readers who like creepy fun.
387: Isekai Tensei: Recruited to Another World by Kenichi (J-Novel Club), illustrated by Nem, is a fantasy action light novel about a reborn hero who just wants a normal life. After Tenma Otori dies, a god offers him a deal: be reborn to help save a dying world, and receive special powers in return. Raised by two retired master adventurers, Tenma grows up hiding just how strong he is, but trouble finds him anyway. It's a solid pick for fans of classic reincarnation adventures.
333: Versus by ONE and Kyotaro Azuma (Kodansha) is a shonen battle fantasy from the creator of One-Punch Man. Centuries ago, the Demon Clan conquered humanity, and the world has been ruled ever since by a Great Demon Lord and his 47 Demon Lords. To fight back, humanity chooses 47 Heroes from around the world, among them Holo, who sets out with his fairy companion, Panepane. It's a must for fans of his work and big, unpredictable fights.
380: Heroine? Saint? No, I'm an All-Works Maid (And Proud of It)! by Atekichi and Keiko (Seven Seas) is a cheerful fantasy comedy. Melody, a maid enthusiast from Japan, is reborn in a new world and finally gets to live her dream as an all-purpose maid, turning cheap leaves into luxury tea and restoring a crumbling mansion in no time, without knowing that she's the near-invincible heroine of an otome game. It's a light, upbeat read for fans of cozy isekai.
381: Cat Companions Maruru and Hachi by Yuri Sonoda (Seven Seas) is a sweet, funny story about two very different cats. Maruru, a pampered house cat, chases a flock of sparrows and ends up lost, where he runs into Hachi, a tough stray who wants nothing to do with a spoiled newcomer on his turf. But after Maruru helps Hachi out of a tight spot, the two team up to survive life on the streets. It's a heartwarming read for cat lovers of all ages.
384: Rai Rai Rai by Yoshiaki (Viz Media) is a wild sci-fi action comedy with a heroine in over her head. Sumire Ichigaya is buried in debt when she's abducted by a UFO. She wakes up with a monstrous new arm and a foul-mouthed voice in her head, and soon she's fighting deadly alien threats just to pay her bills. It's a fast, funny, and energetic read for fans of offbeat action and kaiju-style chaos.
391: Himegasaki Sakurako Is a Hot Mess by Kousuke Yasuda (Seven Seas) is a romantic comedy about a popular girl who can't get her love life right. Sakurako is admired by everyone at school, except by the one boy she likes: her childhood friend Natsuki sees her as nothing more than a friend, and she has to watch him fall for someone else, and every attempt to win him over ends in embarrassment. It's a light, funny read for fans of lovable disaster heroines.
